newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-GUNNELL PULLS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GUNNELL PULLS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Sally Gunnell of Britain, the former world and Olympic champion, pulled out of the world championships on Wednesday after injuring her calf during her first round race on Tuesday.
Gunnell, 31, taking part in her last international competition, was due to run in the 400 hurdles semifinals later on Wednesday.

Team manager Malcolm Arnold confirmed: "She strained a muscle in her left calf during yesterday's race and it was serious enough for her to withdraw from the competition. The doctor confirmed she had done the right thing."

Gunnell, who announced her retirement from international competition earlier this summer, won the Olympic title in 1992 and the world title in 1993 when she also set the previous world record in the event of 52.74 seconds.

It was the second consecutive major championship in which injury has ruined her hopes of success. After missing most of the 1995 season injured, she returned in 1996 but broke down in the Olympic semifinal.
